headline: Imágenes muestran situaciones difíciles de refugiados
content: Las imágenes fueron tomadas en la isla de Lesbos, Idomeni y en algunos campamentos, por 18 fotógrafos miembros del centro fotográfico Refugiados Agregación gracias a haber pasado la difícil prueba, también en señal de esperanza, esa que ya no puede dejar pasar. Pero según la curadora de la exhibición, Marina Koruka, agregada cultural de la Embajada de Grecia en el Perú, aunque estas fotos contienen imágenes de situaciones duras que enfrentan los refugiados, no buscan exponer la miseria humana sino más bien contar historias de resistencia y victoria.

headline: Real Madrid avanza a la final de la UEFA Champions League
content: Su experiencia prevaleció, comentó Cristiano Ronaldo después de que el Real Madrid superara al Atlético de Madrid con un global de 3–2, avanzando así a la final de la Liga de Campeones. Somos el Real Madrid y eso significa muchísimo aquí. Después de perder 2–1 en casa frente al Atlético, necesitarían revertir ese marcador fuera de casa. Sin embargo, un gol temprano de Isco Allí González dio esperanzas al conjunto blanco, permitiéndoles mantener vivo su sueño continental.

headline: Espionage Coronel Claims Former President Requested Political Surveillance
content: New accusations against former president Ollanta Humala continue emerging. Colonel Oswaldo Zapata, who was promoted alongside Humala during their time together in military school, revealed to Perú21 that while serving under Humalas presidency, he was asked to spy on opposition regional political figures.  In 2012, within the Presidential Palace, Humala reportedly requested Zapata gather information about the life, passion, and death of opposing politicians for electoral advantage. When questioned whether specific individuals were targeted, Zapata explained it referred broadly to opponents like those affiliated with Fujimorism and APRA parties. Despite being offered command over intelligence operations, Zapata declined due to his academic training focused more on strategic rather than tactical espionage.

headline: Former Leader Denounces Phone Interceptions During His Term
content: The past allegations regarding phone interceptions conducted during Humala’s administration have been addressed publicly once again. On April 26th, former leader Ollanta Humala commented on these wiretap activities carried out around 2011 concerning investigations linked to terrorist Florindo Flores Halaya. These actions involved members close to him within the National Party. According to Humala, such practices were used improperly beyond legitimate investigative purposes, labeling them as distasteful methods not employed throughout his governance towards other politicians. This controversy also involves claims directed toward former president Alejandro García overseeing these illicit surveillance efforts.

headline: Corruption Cases Reach Over Thirty-Two Thousand
content: Defending public rights organizations presented alarming statistics today highlighting corruption levels across various sectors nationwide. With approximately thirty-two thousand five hundred cases currently active according to data provided by Anti-Corruption Prosecutors Office reports released yesterday, concerns grow surrounding judicial inefficiencies noted by officials including Human Rights Defender Walter Gutierrez. Highlighting systemic issues where reported instances vastly outnumber resolved ones suggests deeper institutional challenges needing urgent attention amidst ongoing economic struggles faced domestically.

headline: DEFENSORA DEL PUEBLO PRESENTÓ PRIMER REPORTE DE LA CORRUPCIÓN EN EL PERÚ
content: La Defensoría del Pueblo presentó ayer el primer reporte de la corrupción en el país con cifras sobre la magnitud de dicho delito en nuestro territorio.   Según datos citados de la Procuraduría Anticorrupción, actualmente existen 32,975 casos de corrupción. Gutierrez destacó especialmente el caso del Poder Judicial, que acumula 695 denuncias por corrupción, lo que él considera insuficiente ante la verdadera situación. Aquí hace falta más política criminal para comprender qué está ocurriendo realmente afirmó. Además, señaló que la corrupción afecta gravemente los derechos humanos debido a las pérdidas económicas significativas causadas por sobornos.
